messages.subject: Re: [vfb-support] questions about further refining NBlast hits
messages.subject_clean: [vfb-support] questions about further refining NBlast hits
messages.body_plain:
Dear Daniel,

I am travelling at the moment, so other VFB people and/or Marta Costa may be able to help, but some quick input inline below. Best,

Greg.

> On 30 Jun 2017, at 18:40, dna.b...@gmail.com wrote:
>
> Thank you for providing this resource. The website is efficiently designed and tutorials are very helpful. I am member of the Fly Functional Connectome project team at the Janelia Research Campus. Using chrimson, we activate neurons in explanted Drosophila brains and look for neurons responding downstream expressing a reporter (ie GCaMP). We hope to use NBLAST to identify the responding neurons. The images depicting the responding neuron are identified using statistical analysis and as a result are less clearly defined as compared to expressing a fluorescent marker directly within a neuron.
>
> After registering the experiment images to the JFRC2 template, I have been using NBLAST to search the database using traces (file.swc simple neurite tracer) from these responding neurons. I have questions about exploring the NBLAST results:
> 1. I can download csv file listing gene name and normalized NBLAST score. I would like to look at these neurons individually but when I search the virtual fly brain stack browser using the gene name (neuron column in csv), the search cannot find the gene name. So, I don’t know how to use the gene name to identify the neuron. When selecting a cluster, the cluster composition lists neurons and gene names which makes further study possible because I can search using the “neuron” name.

You can convert between these two ids using the R fly circuit package. See

http://jefferis.github.io/flycircuit/reference/flycircuit-ids.html

> 2. Is there a means to determine database coverage in a specific brain region? I assume the ‘mirror’ (NBLAST>Upload a tracing) option allows search from the opposite region in the brain. Selecting this option finds different targets. I assume this is due to unequal coverage between right and left sides of the brain?

Marta Costa and I mapped all neurons to a canonical side of the brain (the fly's left, principally defined by soma position). See NBLAST paper in Neuron for details.

> 3. In the virtual fly brain stack browser more advanced queries can be generated. For example, one can search for post and pre-synaptic neurons in the parental classes (ie lobula columna neuron Lcn4) but not individual neurons. Given a list of neurons, is it possible to perform more enquiries looking for terms in the comments or relationships. For example, NBLAST search finds a number of hits and within these hits identify neurons with voxels overlap in the lobula or of a particular neurotransmitter type.

You could use the vfbr package to do some of this at scale. There are not many examples though and you would probably need to ask Rob Court for details of API calls to do what you want.

> 4. I would like to compare the target neuron with the possible hits pairwise. Currently, the 3d/2d views include all hits. Is there a means to include the trace and a single neuron in the same 3d image? Is there a means to download the trace of the hit neurons or the original fluorescent data used to generate the trace so that they can be compared in a composite image?

You can download all the FC neurons and run the NBLAST locally. This snippet will fetch the data:

https://gist.github.com/jefferis/bbaf5d53353b3944c090

> 5. There is a tab (GAL4) to search for GAL4 lines whose expression pattern matches a neuron. Is there a means to search GAL4 lines directly using the a trace (file.swc).

Not online. But you can do it locally if you download the processed GMR data.

Again in R

library(flycircuit)
gmrdps<-read.neuronlistfh("http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/gmrdps/gmrdps.rds", localdir=getOption('flycircuit.datadir'))
#nb should only be necessary to do this next step once
remotesync(gmrdps, download.missing = TRUE)

library(elmr)
# set up for parallel NBLAST across many cores
doMC::registerDoMC(7)
x=nblast_fafb("name:right maxillary ORN VM7d 1138687 GSXEJ", reference=FCWB, mirror=F, db=gmrdps)
summary(x, db=gmrdps)
plot3d(x, db=gmrdps, hits=1)

--
Gregory Jefferis, PhD

messages.subject: Re: CMTK Fiji registration problems
messages.body_plain:
Dear Oliver,

The problem here is not with the same as John Tuthill's issue on Linux -
that was due to a compatibility issue of the CMTK binaries on Linux for
his system.

As you point out in this case the affine and warp registrations ran OK
but no reformatted images were generated. The message exits with value 0
is actually an indication that things went fine with the registration
step (error code 0 generally means no error for programmers).

Your problem is almost certainly to do with the naming conventions of
your input images. The reformat step is stricter than the other ones in
insisting that the the files end with a pair of digits indicating the
channel number. The image file names need to look like this:

myinput01.nrrd
myinput02.nrrd

This is documented on this page

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:registration_gui

linked from

https://github.com/jefferis/fiji-cmtk-gui

Sadly, you will probably find it easiest to correct the naming of your
input files and then rerun everything from scratch rather than trying to
fix the registration folders that you have made with the "wrong" names.

All the best,

Greg.

On 13 Jul 2017, at 12:54, Oliver Barnstedt wrote:

> I recently wanted to run another round of CMTK registrations, and
> everything seemed to run fine, but no ‘reformatted’ directory was
> generated, and I received the following info:

> MYEXEC:  CMD = /Users/Oliver/Documents/Fiji.app/bin/cmtk/warp -v
> --registration-metric nmi --jacobian-weight 0 --fast -e 26
> --grid-spacing 80 --energy-weight 1e-1 --refine 4 --coarsest 8
> --ic-weight 0 --output-intermediate --accuracy 0.4 -o
> Registration/warp/JFRC2_xxxxlexa_2_warp_m0g80c8e1e-1x26r4.list
> Registration/affine/JFRC2_xxxxlexa_2_9dof.list exited with value 0
>
> Ran 0 initial affine registrations of which 0 failed
> Ran 4 affine registrations of which 0 failed
> Ran 4 warp registrations
> Reformatted 0 images
> logout
>
> So the script successfully proceeded to the warp registrations, but
> then somehow “exits with value 0”, and therefore does not begin
> reformatting?
